brief: Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities sales view recapping the GS Tech and Communacopia conference. Bottom line: AI is progressing from infrastructure buildout to measurable enterprise ROI to autonomous agents to physical-world deployment, which the author argues creates a larger and longer-duration opportunity than most investors model. Five themes. One, the conversation moved from capex to ROI, with management framing AI through business outcomes: ServiceNow cites roughly 90% of service cases resolved by AI and about $1bn of value creation, Visa 80% faster product design and build, SAP 30-35% development productivity gains. Two, infrastructure demand visibility keeps companies in early innings, with power and electricity rather than semiconductors the binding constraint: Nvidia reiterates a $3-4tn AI TAM by 2030 and about 70% CY27 growth, Broadcom reaffirms $115bn FY27 and $230bn FY28 AI revenue targets. Three, physical AI is the next demand cycle, which Cadence places 3 to 7 years out. Four, agentic AI becomes the next enterprise software architecture. Five, as foundation models commoditise, proprietary data, context and governance become the moat, so enterprise data owners benefit. These are conference takeaways and company disclosures, not Goldman forecasts.
